title: "Burnout and Mental Health in Pediatric Dental Residency: A Cross-Sectional Survey of Residents and Directors"
format: pdf
authors: "Jack Dumanski and Gregory J. Matthews \\ Center for Data Science and Consulting \\ Loyola University Chicago"
date: "October 23, 2026"
editor: visual
---

# Summary

In this report, we analyzed data within residents and directors, then compared the groups' (*i.e.* residents vs directors) answer selections, informing the difference that various factors can have on a resident's wellbeing and experience in their program, and if the directors have a different perception of what residents face during residency. Out of 81 total tests within the residents group, we found 5 to be significant at the $\alpha$ = 0.05 level. However, none of these were found to be significant after adjusting for multiple hypothesis testing via the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure to control false discovery rate (FDR). Out of 14 tests for directors, nothing was found to be significant either before or after adjustment for multiple hypotheses. When comparing across groups, we found 18 out of the 51 tests performed were significant after the BH adjustment. This means that at least 18 questions saw significant evidence of being answered differently for residents and directors. Results of all tests are reported in the significant findings section, and their significance before and after adjustment will be noted.

# Methods

We tested for associations between questions and differences in proportions across groups (residents vs directors) using Fisher exact tests. Low p-value's indicate significant results.

For questions with multiple parts, we split them into individual questions (e.g. 13a, 13b, 13c...) to see if there were specific responses that were influenced by the grouping variable in question, which was the role (being a resident/director) in the case of cross-comparison, or information like program, experience, etc.

Finally we present data visualizations to summarize the results. Interesting plots and findings were placed in the "significant findings" section with all plots appearing in are in the Appendix.

```{r validation-function, echo=FALSE}
# when trying to cross reference one question (question1) by another grouping variable (question2) 
validation <- function(question1, question2, data){
  df <- data %>%
    transmute(
      response1 = .data[[question1]],
      response2 = .data[[question2]]
    ) %>%
    drop_na()
  
  comparison_res <- df %>%
    group_by(response1, response2) %>%
    summarize(counts = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(response2) %>%
    mutate(percent = counts / sum(counts) * 100) %>%
    ungroup()

  table_comparison <- table(df$response2, df$response1)
#table_hours
  test <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(table_comparison))
  
  if (mean(test$expected <= 5) < 0.8 | any(test$expected < 1)){
    fish_test <- fisher.test(table_comparison, simulate.p.value = TRUE)
    if (fish_test$p.value <= 0.05){
     significant <- TRUE
   }
   else {
      significant <- FALSE
   }
    return(c("question1", "question2", round(fish_test$p.value, digits = 4), significant, "fisher"))
  }
  else{
    if (test$p.value <= 0.05){
     significant <- TRUE
   }
   else {
      significant <- FALSE
   }
    }
  return(c("question1", "question2", round(test$p.value, digits = 4), significant, "chisq"))
}
```

# Results Tables

## Residents Results Table

```{r residents-running, echo=FALSE}

res_results <- data.frame(
  Question1 = character(),
  Question2 = character(),
  P_value = numeric(),
  Significant = logical(), 
  test = character()
)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(question_dic_res))) {

  res_results[i, ] <- validation(
    question1 = question_dic_res$question1s[i],
    question2 = question_dic_res$question2s[i],
    data = f_res_coalesced
  )
}

res_results <- res_results %>%
  mutate(
    Adj_P = round(p.adjust(P_value, method = "BH"), digits = 4),
    Sig_Adj = Adj_P <= 0.05,
    Question1 = question_dic_res$question1s, 
    Question2 = question_dic_res$question2s
  ) %>% arrange(Adj_P)
```

```{r barplot-function, echo=FALSE}
stack_bar <- function(q_reference, q_group, data){
  bar_df <- data %>%
    group_by(.data[[q_reference]], .data[[q_group]]) %>%
    summarize(counts = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    drop_na() %>%
    group_by(.data[[q_group]]) %>%
    mutate(percent = counts / sum(counts) * 100) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  p <- ggplot(bar_df, aes(x = .data[[q_reference]], y = percent, fill = .data[[q_reference]])) +
    geom_col() +
    facet_wrap(vars(.data[[q_group]])) +
    labs(
      title = paste(q_reference, "vs", q_group, sep = " "),
      x = NULL,
      y = "Percent of responses"
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
    )
  return(p)
}

```

# Significant Findings

## Residents Significance

The following relationships were found to be significant:

- Q13d/Q2: Treating patients as impersonal objects and PGY level

- Q13h/Q2: Not caring about what happens to certain patients and PGY level

- Q18/Q11: Working hours/week and desire to quit residency training

- Q16d/Q3: Experiencing sexual harassment and gender

- Q17/Q10: On call days/month and quality of life

```{r, echo = FALSE}
plots_res_sig <- plots_res[c(22, 49, 73, 75, 79)]
walk(plots_res_sig, print)
```

## Directors Significance

No tests in this group were found to be significant.

## Cross-Comparison Significance

Many questions were found to be significant between residents and directors, and below are all the questions that they responded significantly differently to:

- Q3: Gender

- Q12: Recreation hours per week

- Q13a/b/c/f: Feeling emotionally drained, fatigued, strained at work, not caring about what happens to patients

- Q14a/b: Negative impact on marriage, personal healthcare

- Q15a: Experienced discrimination based on gender

- Q19: Frequency of meeting with director

- Q20a/b/d: Frequency of discussing burnout, depression, quitting residency - notably, the only insignificant subquestion concerned suicidal thoughts

- Q21: Presence of standardized criteria for screening burnout & mental health

- Q22a/b/c: Satisfaction with how program manages burnout, depression, suicide

- Q26: Setting for screening (Anonymously vs Confidentially)

```{r}
plots_res_sig <- plots_res[c(2, 7, 8, 9, 10, 13, 17, 18, 21, 30, 31, 32, 34, 35, 36, 37, 38, 50)]
walk(plots_res_sig, print)
```
